question: Since 7 October 2023, Israel has launched a campaign of arbitrary and indiscriminate mass arrests of Palestinian men, women and children1. Nearly 6 000 people have been detained since then and are suffering from poor Israeli prison conditions, ill-treatment and torture2. The majority of them are being held without charge or trial under so-called administrative detention.

On 18 December 2023, Munther Amira was arrested at his home in the Aida refugee camp (Bethlehem). On 31 December an administrative detention order was issued against him, which remains in force to this day3. Munther is a human rights defender and is also the Chair of the board of the Aida Youth Centre, a community organisation that supports children and young people in the refugee camp.
He suffers from hypertension and the denial of adequate medical treatment poses a serious threat to Munther’s life. 1.
Does the EU intend to demand an investigation into his case and his immediate release in the absence of concrete offences or tangible evidence?
Will the EU do anything about the restriction on visits by lawyers, relatives and the International Red Cross, which is further aggravating the already dangerous situation of Palestinian prisoners?
answer: The EU remains concerned about the extensive recourse by Israel to administrative detention without formal charge. Under international law, detainees have the right to be informed about the charges underlying their detention and to have the legality of their detention determined without undue delay, as well as the right to legal assistance, due process, and a fair trial.

The EU continues to call for the full respect of international human rights obligations towards all prisoners, including in the context of arrest, interrogation, and detention. These issues are regularly raised by the EU in the dialogue with Israel.
